chapter: Sam Morgan, La Vida and Ridgley
title: Ridgley's band at the Plantation: personnel and guitarist Sales
summary: After Celestin and Ridgley split, Williams joined Ridgley's band at the Plantation; talk of its players, Handy, and guitarist Sales.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Yeah, Raymond Brown. He would play. Then Handley, he would get on the drum, you know. Play a waltz, you know, until I come back. Yeah. Then after I left there in 29, around 20, yeah, I don't know, around 27, I played there about a year, 28. Celestine and Ridgely's band broke up then. That's when the band split. Well, I went with Ridgely. See, Ridgely made up a band. See, I went with Ridgely, paid with Ridgely down at Pete Hoyman's place. What do you call it? Planetation? Yeah. Planetation. That's right. I worked there, we worked there for about a year, and then we just jobbed around, you know, just gigged around. Yeah. That band consists of me, Ridgely, Emma Barry. Tip된 stuff there.
Shots, Handy, Sales. What did Handy play in those days? Alto and clarinet. Did he play much clarinet then? Oh, lots of clarinet. I can't think of this one. I'm a mic now.
About sales, how did he rate among the guitar players and banjo players?
He used to put on all these hats, changed hats all the time. He had about ten or twelve hats at night. Not played that many bass for that. I was playing with them.
You don't have to be afraid to talk, I don't know, you're out there and there.

Yeah, he was. Jimmy Jones? Jimmy Jones. Jimmy. Jimmy. Jimmy. You forgot? Yeah, Jimmy. You know what I was trying to think was playing with us at Pete Ornans, played bass, but we might not have a bass then.
How did Sales rate in those days? He was a nice, fine guitar player. I just wondered who would be among the best guitar players in town. Oh yeah, he was fine, yes indeed.
